entities.name: Matěj Rejsek
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Matěj Rejsek (c. 1445 – July 1, 1506) emerged as a preeminent Bohemian architect, stonemason, and sculptor during the late 15th and early 16th centuries, becoming a pivotal figure in the dissemination and evolution of the Late Gothic style within Central Europe. His architectural genius, deeply rooted in the Parler tradition yet infused with innovative elements, profoundly shaped the urban landscape of Prague and other Bohemian towns, embodying the final flourishing of Gothic artistry before the full advent of the Renaissance. Rejsek's work represents a critical transitional phase, demonstrating mastery of intricate vaulting and elaborate stonework that defined the era's grand ecclesiastical and civic constructions, particularly under the patronage of King Vladislaus II Jagiellon.

Rejsek's most celebrated commission was the completion of the Powder Tower (Prašná brána) in Prague, a monumental city gate begun in 1475. He took over construction in 1478, designing its elaborate sculptural decoration and intricate vaulting, a project that solidified his reputation as a master builder. Beyond Prague, Rejsek designed and oversaw the construction of significant ecclesiastical structures, including the vaulting of St. Barbara's Church in Kutná Hora, a UNESCO World Heritage site, where he introduced a complex web-vaulting system that pushed the boundaries of Gothic engineering. His work also encompassed the reconstruction of the vaulting in the Church of Our Lady before Týn in Prague's Old Town Square, following a fire, showcasing his ability to adapt and enhance existing structures with innovative Gothic forms.

entities.summary:
Matěj Rejsek (c. 1450, Prostějov – July 1, 1506, Prague) emerged as a preeminent Czech master builder, stonemason, and architect whose monumental works defined the late Gothic aesthetic in Bohemia during a pivotal period of recovery and artistic renewal following the Hussite Wars. His career, spanning the reigns of George of Poděbrady and particularly Vladislaus II Jagiellon, marked a decisive transition from the High Gothic traditions of the Parler workshop to a more ornate, intricate, and distinctly Central European Late Gothic style. Rejsek's contributions are central to understanding the architectural identity of Prague and Kutná Hora at the turn of the 16th century, placing him among the most significant artistic figures of his era in the region.

Rejsek's most celebrated achievement is the Powder Tower (Prašná brána) in Prague, initiated in 1475. This imposing city gate, originally conceived as a royal entrance, showcases his mastery of complex vaulting systems, intricate stone carving, and a rich sculptural program that integrated heraldic symbols and royal effigies, including those of Vladislaus II. Although left unfinished by Rejsek, the tower's design profoundly influenced later Bohemian architecture. Concurrently, from 1489, he also contributed significantly to the construction of the magnificent St. Barbara's Church in Kutná Hora, designing the intricate vaulting of its chancel, a testament to his structural ingenuity and decorative flair that continued the work begun by Jan Parléř.
